answer: Sequential Physical Delivery Ledger. Each identity must receive a small physical token (a stamped opal blank) shipped to a verified street address, and registration activates only when the token's serial is entered back. Because one operator physically cannot receive thousands of separate mailpieces at addresses they do not control, mass registration collapses. A timber crate of blanks costs little, but each forged identity requires a distinct deliverable address and a returned serial, so per-identity cost becomes real postage, address leasing, and handling labor.
